bounded_correction: Preregistered survey experiments found immediate changes in election confidence, fraud beliefs, and factual accuracy after factual election-security messages; persistence was mixed.

bounded_correction: Removing a first-page Reject all button increased acceptance of injected cookie-consent notices by 22.0 percentage points for barriers and 23.1 points for banners.
study_design: Counterbalanced within-subject field experiment during normal browsing; 40 United States Chrome users; eight injected interfaces.
observed_endpoint: Binary acceptance of injected cookie-consent notices under first-page button-prominence manipulations.
key_limitation: No regulatory-ban, data-disclosure, legal-compliance, political-behaviour, or agency endpoint; no causal estimate of preference alignment; small non-probability sample.

bounded_correction: Of 1,037,113 appearances of duplicated multimedia that received an FMT label at least once, 612,855 appearances (59%) did not carry that label.

observed_endpoint: Conditional share of duplicated-media appearances lacking a Forwarded Many Times label.
key_limitation: No counterfactual estimate of cost, delay, reach, virality, encryption, or harm; selected public groups are not representative of WhatsApp or private chats.

observed_endpoint: Immediate recognition of specifically taught manipulation techniques; laboratory discernment measures were generally but not universally positive.
key_limitation: No durability beyond 24 hours, actual sharing, transfer to untaught techniques or cultures, election behaviour, pluralism, reflective agency, or agency-transfer endpoint.

bounded_correction: Across four consumer IoT systems in 2019, researchers received relevant personal data in three of four exercises; none enabled import to a second provider or direct provider-to-provider transfer.
